overview: This House resolution sets the ground rules for House debate on three law enforcement bills. They are H.R. 2240, which would require the Attorney General to report on violent attacks against police officers; H.R. 2243, which would expand rules allowing current and retired officers to carry concealed weapons; and H.R. 2255, which would let federal officers buy their retired service weapons. For each bill, it allows one hour of debate split between the leaders of the Judiciary Committee, adopts that committee's revised version, waives procedural objections, and allows one motion to recommit (a final attempt to send the bill back to committee) but no other amendments. The House adopted it on May 14, 2025.
for: Supporters say it lets the House move promptly to vote on bills aimed at protecting and supporting law enforcement officers.
against: Critics say it limits debate to an hour and blocks members from offering amendments to the three bills.
